name: Hydrogen-capable and ammonia-fired gas turbines
applications: transition of gas fleets to hydrogen
principle: Gas turbines burn natural gas blended with hydrogen, and developers are working toward pure hydrogen and ammonia. Mitsubishi Power has run a 30% hydrogen blend on an M501JAC and supplied two M501JAC units (about 840 MW) to the Intermountain Power Project in Utah with a 100% hydrogen target by 2045; GE says its 7HA can burn up to 50% hydrogen.

process_steps.name: Hydrogen supply and blending with natural gas
Combustion in a modified or multi-cluster combustor

performance.metric: hydrogen blend at IPP Renewed start-up
performance.basis: two M501JAC, about 840 MW; 100% hydrogen target by 2045

source.note: Turbomachinery Magazine, Mitsubishi Power delivers 30% hydrogen-fuel gas turbines to IPP Renewed in Utah, 1 August 2023
GE Vernova, 7HA gas turbine page, read 25 October 2026

IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'H₂ blending in natural gas turbine' 9 (2025); 'Pure h₂ gas turbine' 8 (2025); 'Co-firing of ammonia in gas turbines' 5 (2025)

advantages: Cuts CO2 as hydrogen share rises
limitations: Pure hydrogen and ammonia combustion are not yet commercial
Hydrogen supply and storage are separate projects
